026-B02.evidence: Both M glyphs have the same two upright peaks and central valley; the variation from curved to straight feet does not establish a second alphabet. The hook at the left and pointed right arrowhead, 26, lower g/nu and terminal stop are visible. Adopt plain M consistently; math delimiters and the second reader's edge comment are editorial.

026-B03.decision: retain first with explicit scope uncertainty
026-B03.evidence: The D-shaped right cluster is crossed by diagonal and looping cancellation strokes. The bottom heavy stroke reaches toward the M, but the upper M body remains clear. Root blind review retains cancellation of MD first while explicitly allowing M to remain live; the right letter itself remains tentative. The following hyphen and graphes are live.

026-B04.evidence: The short n and separate high bent b are clear; no dot follows nb. The second reading agrees and adds only an editorial crop-edge comment.

026-B06.evidence: There is one de group. Its d and upper e loop remain intact, while the thick low cancellation covers the small final sign. Retain de with uncertain cancelled s; no separate second des is visible. The second reading agrees textually and comments on the strike.

026-B07.decision: retain letters and bar; consistent capital M
026-B07.evidence: Each lower G has a short inward/lower return, distinguishing it from the open inclusion curve; the first G has one detached prime. The long bar covers M and its G index. Plain M is the consistent rendering of this capital; the second reader's C alternative and edge comments do not displace these visible strokes.
